source.title: Identifying Interpretable Visual Features in Artificial and Biological Neural Systems
source.authors: David A. Klindt; S. Sanborn; Francisco Acosta; Frédéric Poitevin; N. Miolane

page_placements.theme: Superposition and interpretability measures change over training

record.tranche_reason: The study measures interpretability of individual neurons and non-axis-aligned activation directions using an automated image-similarity metric and in-silico psychophysics, rather than the original neuron-specific visualization method.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that K-Means directions have higher interpretability than individual neurons, and describes psychophysics comparisons across similarity metrics and task difficulties. Results cited from other studies are not recorded as findings of this study. Biological neural-data analyses are excluded because the listed claim versions concern trained networks.
record.test_reason: The study scores how coherent individual ResNet50 neurons' top-activating images are, compared with K-Means directions. This bears on V1, since low-II neurons have incoherent MEIs. It also bears on V7 through metric choice and activation-range (difficulty) manipulations. It frames itself as a test of superposition, but it never tests the cause (more sparse features than neurons), so V3 is not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that their LPIPS-based automated metric is a reasonable proxy for human judgments in early layers. They find K-Means directions more interpretable than individual neurons in CNNs and in macaque and human visual data, which they call 'consistent with' superposition. They add that pairwise feature synergy exists and that the gap appears even in untrained models (Appendix H), with training shifting semantics toward labels.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses an automated LPIPS-based interpretability index and in-silico psychophysics, and identifies directions primarily with K-Means; it does not reproduce the original feature-visualization analysis of a specific neuron.
record.method_sensitivity: Interpretability results vary with the image-similarity metric and LPIPS layer; in-silico psychophysics accuracy varies with task difficulty and semantic level.

fits_no_version.finding: K-Means (and SAE) directions in activation space have higher interpretability than neuron axes, even when K exceeds N (K=512 vs N=256, no II change).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In vision CNNs, non-axis-aligned activation directions are more interpretable than individual neurons.

fits_no_version.finding: The neuron-vs-cluster interpretability gap exists at initialization. Training shifts predictability from color toward label semantics.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the tested ResNet50, the relative interpretability advantage of activity clusters is already present at initialization, while training shifts which semantic level best predicts responses.

fits_no_version.finding: Neurons more co-active with the rest of the population have lower II (App. E, Fig. 16C).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Neurons that fire alone are more monosemantic (privileged-basis account).

record.problems: The main CNN comparisons focus on layer 1 of one ResNet50 trained on CIFAR-10. Several outcomes are shown only in figures without exact reported values. The automated interpretability measure is validated against human judgments most successfully for early layers, with AUC up to 0.71 and acknowledged room for improvement. The study does not quantify the proportion of polysemantic neurons or test the capacity-pressure mechanism.
record.rows_left_out: Excluded analyses of biological neural recordings, disentanglement, robustness, activation-manifold geometry, and correlations because they do not directly test the trained-network behaviors in the listed versions. Also excluded results cited from prior studies.

untested.parts: No share or count of polysemantic neurons is reported. InceptionV1 and the specific cat/car neuron are not examined. Only layer 1 of a CIFAR-10 ResNet50 is analysed.
Entirely untested; there are no language models.
The causal claim (more sparse features than neurons, packed together) is not tested. The higher interpretability of non-axis directions is only called 'consistent with' superposition.
Entirely untested. The untrained-model gap is not a test with capacity controlled.
Entirely untested; no activation-function, architecture or regularization comparisons are made.
Entirely untested; canonical polysemantic neurons are not re-examined.
Alternative definitions of polysemanticity and LLM-style explanation scoring are not compared.

missing.what: Median split of neurons into low-II and high-II groups. K-Means on either subset raises II, and low-II neurons are explicitly called uninterpretable.
Qualitative MEIs of neurons at II quantiles, showing incoherent top images for low-II neurons.
Pairwise synergy: most neuron pairs lower II, but some sums are more interpretable; high-II neurons have lower maximal synergy.

record.verdict_notes: The core CNN evidence is one CIFAR-10 ResNet50 at layer 1, mostly figure-only, with no uncertainty reported. The record's V3 'supports' label is dropped: finding interpretable non-axis directions does not test whether polysemanticity is caused by feature packing. The untrained-model gap, if anything, complicates a purely learned-superposition reading. Biological analyses are correctly excluded.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not report a count or share of neurons responding to unrelated inputs, nor analyze the specific InceptionV1 neuron in the claim.
Transformer language models, MLP neurons, and token or context responses are not studied.

The study tests whether non-axis-aligned directions are more interpretable than neuron axes, but does not test whether this is caused by having more sparse features than neurons or by capacity pressure.
The study does not test initialization, regularization, or training noise as causes of polysemantic neurons when capacity is sufficient.

It does not compare activation functions, architectures, or regularization to measure changes in the share of polysemantic neurons, nor test whether that share can be lowered without substantial performance loss.
The study does not examine canonical polysemantic neurons to determine whether their apparently mixed inputs share a feature or related job.
The study varies image-similarity metrics, LPIPS layers, and psychophysics difficulty, but does not compare alternative explanation-scoring procedures beyond those reported.

rows.subject: ResNet50 pre-trained on CIFAR-10
rows.operation_detail: Compared the interpretability index (II) of layer-1 neuron axes with K-Means directions.
rows.measure: Interpretability index (II), based on pairwise similarity of top MEIs
rows.baseline: Individual neuron II; exact value not stated
rows.note: The paper states that K-Means directions have higher II than individual neurons and the tested baselines. The number is reported for K-Means directions, not separately for neuron axes.
rows.check: The value is the K-Means mean (-0.0159), not the neuron II. The relevant result is that neuron II is lower than direction II (Fig. 3). This bears on V1 only indirectly: it shows neurons with less coherent top images, not a count of neurons with unrelated inputs. It does not test V3's causal claim, so the V3 link is removed.

source_check.problem: Value -0.0159 is the K-Means mean, not neuron II; the row says so. The text does not tie it to K=256, and Fig. 3 shows neurons below directions.

source_check.notes: All values except the K-Means mean II (-0.0159) are figure only. The activation-range drop (Fig. 5) is a designed difficulty effect that also hits K-Means directions; no neuron is ever classified as polysemantic, so the V1 and V7 links are indirect. The untrained-model result is in App. H/Fig. 19, though the main text says App. G. The text and the Fig. 3 caption disagree on which panel varies the LPIPS layer.

statements.problem: Numbers and conditions match: layer 1, N=256 neurons, K-Means mean II -0.0159, ordering holds on all metrics and difficulties. Psychophysics (R3-R5) used K in {128, 256, 512}, not only 256, but K made no difference. The statement already calls the evidence indirect.

Correct as stated: accuracy falls as queries move to central quantiles (Fig. 5). The drop is a designed difficulty effect, and it hits K-Means directions too, but the statement makes no claim against that.
K-Means more coherent than neurons is right. Most neuron pairs have negative synergy, and a good fraction of sums are more interpretable (Fig. 6C).

The sentence about this study is right: accuracy falls toward central quantiles under colour, LPIPS and label similarity (Fig. 5, figure only). Directions lose accuracy too and stay ahead of neurons; the paper calls the drop expected.

statements.correction: Either drop R7, or add: arXiv:2310.11431, ResNet50 CIFAR-10 layer 1: II rises with the LPIPS layer used for scoring; neurons stay below K-Means directions at every LPIPS layer (R7; figure only).
statements.problem: The item cites R7 from this study but never states this study's result. Every sentence and the 'why' field are about other studies, so the citation is left hanging.
Matches the text: the ordering holds 'independently of the LPIPS layer' and across metrics and difficulties, and the advantage is largest for colour and smaller for label similarity.
The statement about this study is right; the stated differences (CIFAR-10 ResNet50, LPIPS II and psychophysics, K-Means directions, figure only) are correct.
Text says II increases with the LPIPS layer used (figure only).
Matches App. H, Fig. 19: gap present at initialization; semantics shift from colour to label with training. (The main text wrongly points to App. G, but the statement gives no locator.)

reader_labels.reason: The study does not quantify how many neurons respond to unrelated inputs or test the cited InceptionV1 example; its evidence is an interpretability-score comparison in a limited setting (R1, R3-R5).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Non-axis-aligned K-Means directions score higher than neuron axes on the study's interpretability measures, supporting the existence of more interpretable directions beyond individual neurons (R1, R3-R5).

reader_labels.reason: Scores and direction-versus-neuron advantages depend on the similarity metric and difficulty; the paper reports a trend with LPIPS layer, a larger gain for color than higher-level semantics, and reduced accuracy at greater difficulty (R3-R5, R7).
